title: Early metabolic defects in dexamethasone-exposed and undernourished intrauterine growth restricted rats.
ehr_evidence: The study used experimental rat models (Sprague-Dawley rats) with physiological, morphometric, and transcriptomic measurements; no electronic or computerised health records were used.
summary: An experimental animal study modeling intrauterine growth restriction in rat pups through prenatal dexamethasone exposure or maternal undernutrition, revealing early physiologic, morphologic, and transcriptomic metabolic defects before catch-up growth.
key_findings: Birth body weight was reduced by approximately 13% in DEX and 17% in UN pups (p<0.0001) versus controls
At PND7, DEX and UN pups remained 13% (p<0.005) and 24% (p<0.0001) lighter than controls with no catch-up growth
Hepatic Pck1 mRNA increased by 46±19% (p<0.05) in DEX and 53±7% (p<0.05) in UN pups; G6pc increased by 101±35% (p<0.05) in DEX and 85±20% (p<0.05) in UN
Basal hyperglycaemia at PND21: DEX 6.9±0.1 mmol/l (p<0.005) and UN 6.8±0.1 mmol/l (p<0.02) versus 6.2±0.2 mmol/l controls
GTT AUC increased in DEX (868±27 mmol/L*min, p<0.0001) and UN (870±26 mmol/L*min, p<0.0001) versus 693±16 controls
Pancreatic islet number reduced to 62±5 (DEX, p<0.01) and 52±4 (UN, p<0.0001) versus 82±4 controls
Mean islet size reduced to 146±26 mm2 (DEX, p<0.0001) and 161±79 mm2 (UN, p<0.02) versus 191±78 mm2 controls
Whole pancreas insulin content decreased in DEX (12.6±1.0 mg) and UN (13.7±1.2 mg, p<0.01) versus 20.3±1.5 mg controls
UN pups showed reduced epididymal white adipose tissue (44±5 mg, p<0.01) versus 71±7 mg controls
DEX pups showed attenuated insulin sensitivity on ITT whereas UN pups showed decreased glucose-induced insulin secretion
captured_features: hepatic Pck1 and G6pc mRNA and protein
gene expression in pancreatic islets, liver, and adipose tissue
white and brown adipose tissue weight
study_design: experimental animal model study (controlled experimental design with dexamethasone and undernutrition models versus controls)
population: Sprague-Dawley rat pups (male and female) studied at postnatal days 0, 7, 21, and 28; male pups used for physiological analyses
exposure_domain: maternal prenatal dexamethasone (synthetic glucocorticoid) exposure and maternal undernutrition
limitations: Rat model may not fully replicate human metabolic programming and IUGR
Only male pups used for physiological analyses, limiting generalisability to females
Insulin tolerance test is less sensitive than standard euglycaemic hyperinsulinemic clamps
Small per-group sample sizes in several analyses
